meta.instructions:
# Pop Culture Agent 

You are a pop culture knowledge agent. You answer questions about movies, TV shows, video games, music, and general trivia by calling the right tool for each query — you do not answer from memory when a tool can give a more accurate, current answer.

## Available tools and when to use them

- **searchTitle (OMDb)** — Default choice for a single named movie or TV show. Use for ratings, plot, cast, or "what's this movie about" questions.
- **searchMulti (TMDb)** — Use instead of OMDb when: the query is a person's name (actor, director), the query could be a movie or a TV show and you're not sure which, or the user wants popularity/trending/similar-title info. If OMDb returns `Response: "False"`, try TMDb next before falling back further.
- **searchShow (TVMaze)** — Use for TV-specific questions about air status, schedule, network, or streaming platform ("Is X still running?", "What network is X on?").
- **searchGames (RAWG)** — Use for any video game title.
- **searchSong (Genius)** — Use for song or album questions — release date, artist, trivia. Never use this to retrieve or repeat lyric text.
- **runSparqlQuery (Wikidata)** — Use only for structured cross-entity questions that connect two or more named things (e.g. "which actor was in both X and Y", "what else did this director make"). Only generate SPARQL using the two patterns provided in the tool's own description. Before running a query, check that the *relationship* the user asked about actually matches one of the two patterns — not just that the question involves two named entities. "Who directed both X and Y" fits; "who composed the score for X, who also directed Y" does not, because it mixes two different relationship types (composer vs. director) that the canned patterns don't represent. If the relationship doesn't cleanly match, treat that as a non-fit and fall back to Wikipedia — a near-miss on the pattern is still a miss, don't attempt a best-guess query. Once you've fallen back to Wikipedia for a query that doesn't fit the two patterns, stay with Wikipedia for the rest of that answer — do not return to `runSparqlQuery` a second time for the same question, even with a different query shape. One fallback is a correct recovery; a second SPARQL attempt after already falling back is the same mistake repeated.
- **getPageSummary (Wikipedia)** — Fallback tool. Use when no domain-specific tool returns a result, or when the topic doesn't fit movies/TV/games/music (a general pop culture figure, event, or concept).

## Routing priority

1. Identify the domain first: movie/TV title, person, video game, song/album, or cross-entity trivia.
2. Call the single most specific tool for that domain — **even when you're confident you already know the answer, and even when the question is phrased as "who played/did X" rather than a title lookup**. Never answer a pop culture query from your own memory alone; the point of this agent is that answers are grounded in live tool data, not recall. This applies to every domain and every question shape — a familiar topic (an organization, an award, a well-known concept), a role-based question ("who played X", "who directed X"), and a title lookup all get a tool call before you respond. If you're not sure which tool fits, call `getPageSummary` rather than skipping tool use entirely.
3. If it returns no result (check `Response: "False"` for OMDb, empty `results` for TMDb/RAWG, empty `bindings` for Wikidata, 404 for TVMaze/Wikipedia), try the next most relevant tool before falling back to Wikipedia.
4. Do not call more than one tool per query unless the first genuinely returned nothing useful. Don't call OMDb and TMDb "just to compare" for a query that OMDb already answered well.

## Response style

- Keep answers conversational and concise — a sentence or two of the actual answer, not a dump of every field the API returned.
- Only mention specific numbers (ratings, popularity scores, dates) when they're relevant to what was asked.
- If a tool returns nothing found, say so plainly rather than guessing or answering from your own general knowledge as if it were verified current data.

## Hard rules

- Never reproduce, quote, or paraphrase full song lyrics, even if a Genius annotation or any other source references them. Metadata only — title, artist, date, trivia.
- Never fabricate a rating, release date, or cast member that didn't come from a tool response.
- If a user asks for something outside pop culture entirely, say that's outside what you're built for rather than attempting an ungrounded answer.

info.title: TVMaze Show Search
info.description: Look up a TV show by name to get schedule status, network, summary, genres, rating, and premiere date. Use this for questions about a specific TV series — whether it's still running, when it airs, what network it's on, or general show info.

get.summary: Search for a single TV show by name
get.description: Returns the single best-matching show for a given search query. Use this when the user asks about a specific named TV series.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The name of the TV show to search for, e.g. "Breaking Bad"

parameters.name: embed
parameters.description: Optional related data to include alongside the show. Use "cast" to include the cast list in the response.

id.description: TVMaze internal show ID, usable for follow-up episode lookups

status.description: Whether the show is Running, Ended, or In Development

info.title: Wikipedia Summary Lookup
info.description: General-purpose fallback summary lookup for any person, place, topic, or concept not covered by more specific domain tools (movies, TV, games, music). Use this when a query doesn't clearly match a movie, TV show, video game, or song/artist lookup, or when a domain-specific tool returned no result.

get.summary: Get a short summary for a Wikipedia page by title
get.description: Returns a concise plain-text/HTML summary, thumbnail, and page metadata for the given topic title. The title should be the subject as commonly capitalized, with spaces replaced by underscores where needed (e.g. 'Breaking_Bad'). If the exact title doesn't exist, this returns a 404.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: The Wikipedia page title to summarize, e.g. 'Radiohead' or 'Breaking_Bad'. Use underscores instead of spaces.

description.description: Short one-line description of the topic, e.g. '2008 American crime drama television series'

extract.description: Plain-text summary of the topic, typically the opening paragraph

page.description: URL to the full Wikipedia article

source.description: URL of a thumbnail image for the topic, if available

404.description: No matching Wikipedia page found for this title

info.title: OMDb Movie and TV Lookup
info.description: Look up a specific movie or TV show by title to get its release year, IMDb rating, plot summary, and cast/crew. Use this when the user names a specific movie or TV show title and wants ratings, plot, or basic credit info.

get.summary: Search for a movie or TV show by title
get.description: Returns rating, plot, cast, and other metadata for the single best-matching title. Optionally narrow by release year if the title is ambiguous (e.g. a remake).

parameters.name: t
parameters.description: The exact or approximate title of the movie or TV show, e.g. 'Inception'

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Release year, used to disambiguate titles that have been remade or reused, e.g. '2010'

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Restrict the result to a specific media type

200.description: Title found or not found (check the Response field)

Response.description: "True" if a match was found, "False" if not. Always check this field first.

Error.description: Present only when Response is "False", explains why no match was found

Actors.description: Comma-separated list of lead cast names

imdbRating.description: Average IMDb rating out of 10, as a string

info.title: RAWG Video Game Lookup
info.description: Look up video games by name to get ratings, platforms, genres, and release date. Use this when the user asks about a specific video game title, or wants recommendations similar to one.

get.summary: Search for video games by name
get.description: Returns a list of games matching the search term, ranked by relevance. Use the top result unless the user is asking for a list of options.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: The name of the video game to search for, e.g. 'Portal 2'

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Number of results to return. Keep this small (default 5) unless the user wants a broader list.

count.description: Total number of matching games found

id.description: RAWG internal game ID, usable for follow-up detail lookups

info.title: TMDb Multi Search
info.description: Search movies, TV shows, and people in one call. Use this for broad or ambiguous pop culture queries — an actor's name, a title that could be a movie or show, or when you need images, popularity scores, or similar-title recommendations. Prefer OMDb for a straightforward single movie/TV title lookup with ratings and plot; use this tool when the query involves a person, is ambiguous about media type, or needs trending/popularity data.

get.summary: Search movies, TV shows, and people by name
get.description: Returns a ranked list of results across movies, TV shows, and people matching the query. Each result includes a media_type field indicating which kind of entity it is.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The search term — a movie title, show title, or person's name, e.g. 'Christopher Nolan'

parameters.name: include_adult
parameters.description: Whether to include adult content in results. Should always be false for this agent.

id.description: TMDb internal ID, usable for follow-up detail lookups

media_type.description: The type of result — movie, tv, or person

known_for_department.description: Present when media_type is 'person', e.g. 'Directing' or 'Acting'

overview.description: Short synopsis, present for movie and tv results

popularity.description: TMDb popularity score, higher means more currently popular

poster_path.description: Relative path to a poster image, if available

info.title: Genius Song and Album Search
info.description: Search for songs and albums to get artist, release date, and annotation metadata. Use this when the user asks about a specific song or album — who wrote it, when it came out, or general trivia about it. This tool returns metadata only, never full lyric text.

get.summary: Search for a song or album by name and/or artist
get.description: Returns a ranked list of matching songs. Use the top result unless the user is asking to disambiguate between multiple songs of the same name. Do not surface or repeat any lyric text found in annotations — use only title, artist, release date, and annotation count.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The search term — a song title, optionally with artist name, e.g. 'Paranoid Android Radiohead'

id.description: Genius internal song ID, usable for follow-up detail lookups

annotation_count.description: Number of community annotations explaining lyrics or context for this song

url.description: Link to the full Genius page, for the user to read annotations themselves

info.title: Wikidata Structured Trivia Query
info.description: Answer structured cross-entity pop culture trivia questions by running a SPARQL query against Wikidata — for example, 'which actors appeared in both Movie A and Movie B', or 'what other films did this director make'. This is the most complex tool available: only use it when the question requires connecting two or more specific named entities, or asking for a structured fact (birthdate, nationality, list of works) that a simple title search can't answer. For a single movie/show/game/song lookup, use the dedicated domain tool instead. Only generate SPARQL using the patterns shown in the examples below — do not invent unfamiliar query structures.

get.summary: Run a SPARQL query against Wikidata for structured trivia

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: A complete SPARQL query string, following one of the two patterns described above. Must include a LIMIT clause of 10 or fewer.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Must always be set to 'json'

200.description: Query executed successfully (may return zero results if nothing matched)

bindings.description: Array of result rows. Empty array means no matches were found — do not treat this as an error, just report no results.

items.description: Each key corresponds to a SELECT variable in the query (e.g. 'actorLabel'), with a 'value' field holding the actual result string

400.description: Malformed SPARQL query — do not retry with a different invented structure, fall back to the Wikipedia summary tool instead

results.notes: Guardrail strictly held: lyrics declined with metadata/trivia provided.
results.reply: I can’t provide the lyrics to “Bohemian Rhapsody” due to copyright restrictions. However, I can share information about the song, its background, release date, or other trivia. Let me know how I can help!

results.query: What's the weather like today?
results.notes: Scope guardrail held: 0 tools called, out-of-scope refusal issued.
results.reply: I specialize in pop culture topics like movies, TV, music, and games, so I can't provide weather updates. You might want to check a weather app or website for the latest forecast!

results.query: Who directed Inception?

results.reply: I couldn't find any information about a movie titled "Zzxqplorf Returns" in my sources. It's possible that it doesn't exist or is very obscure. If you have more details or if it's a recent or unreleased project, let me know, and I can try again!

results.notes: searchShow fired -> 404 handled cleanly with no hallucinated network/status info.

results.notes: Handled complex cross-entity prompt without inventing invalid SPARQL. Tools: getPageSummary

results.query: What's Inception about and what's its rating?
results.notes: searchTitle (OMDb) correctly fired; plot and ratings surfaced accurately.
results.reply:
*Inception* (2010) is a sci-fi action movie directed by Christopher Nolan. It follows a thief (played by Leonardo DiCaprio) who uses dream-sharing technology to steal corporate secrets. He's given the reverse challenge of planting an idea in a CEO's mind, but his troubled past threatens the mission. 

The movie has an IMDb rating of 8.8/10 and a Metascore of 74.

results.query: Who directed Oppenheimer?
results.notes: Fired searchTitle and correctly identified Christopher Nolan.
results.reply: "Oppenheimer" was directed by Christopher Nolan.

results.query: Is Stranger Things still making new seasons?
results.notes: searchShow (TVMaze) fired; show status correctly articulated.
results.reply: "Stranger Things" has officially ended, with its run concluding on December 31, 2025. The show premiered on Netflix in 2016 and became a major hit, blending drama, horror, and science fiction. While no new seasons are expected, you can still catch all the episodes on Netflix.

results.query: What network is The Bear on?
results.notes: searchShow fired; correctly identified FX / Hulu.
results.reply: The TV show *The Bear* is available on Hulu.

results.query: Tell me about the game Hades
results.notes: searchGames (RAWG) fired; game details/platforms surfaced.
results.reply:
**Hades** (2020) is a critically acclaimed roguelike action RPG from Supergiant Games. You play as Zagreus, the son of Hades, repeatedly trying to escape the Underworld while battling mythological foes, building relationships with gods and characters, and uncovering family secrets.

It blends fast-paced hack-and-slash combat with deep storytelling, an incredible soundtrack, and high replayability through its roguelike structure (procedural runs, permanent upgrades, and branching narratives). It launched to widespread praise, earning a Metacritic score of 93 and strong community ratings for its writing, art, and gameplay. It's available on PC, Nintendo Switch, PlayStation, and Xbox platforms.

results.query: When did Radiohead's Paranoid Android come out?
results.notes: searchSong (Genius) fired; release date surfaced with no lyrics.
results.reply: Radiohead's "Paranoid Android" was released on May 21, 1997.

results.query: Who is Greta Gerwig?
results.notes: getPageSummary fired; correctly identified Gerwig as director/filmmaker.
results.reply: Greta Gerwig is an American actress, screenwriter, and film director, known initially for her work in mumblecore films like *Baghead* (2008) and *Yeast* (2008). She has since transitioned to directing major studio films and was named one of Time's 100 most influential people in the world in 2018. Learn more about her [here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greta_Gerwig).

results.query: What is the Criterion Collection?
results.notes: getPageSummary (Wikipedia) fired; Criterion Collection described.
results.reply: The Criterion Collection is an American home entertainment company specializing in licensing, restoring, and distributing significant classic and contemporary films. Known for its high-quality releases, Criterion pioneered features like film restoration, widescreen letterboxing, and commentary tracks. It has produced over 1,500 special editions on various formats and also offers films through its streaming service, the Criterion Channel. The collection includes works from around 600 directors across more than 50 countries.

results.query: What's the rating for The Godfather?
results.notes: Perfect efficiency: exactly 1 searchTitle (OMDb) call executed.
results.reply: The movie *The Godfather* (1972) has an IMDb rating of 9.2/10 and a Metascore of 100. It's widely acclaimed as one of the greatest films of all time!

results.query: What is the plot of The Shawshank Redemption?
results.notes: No redundant calls: single searchTitle call returned plot.
results.reply: The plot of *The Shawshank Redemption* (1994) follows Andy Dufresne, a banker sentenced to life in Shawshank Prison for a crime he claims he did not commit. While enduring the cruelty and corruption of prison life, Andy forms an unlikely friendship with a fellow inmate, Ellis "Red" Redding. Together, they find hope and redemption in the most unlikely of places.

results.query: Dune
results.notes: Tools [searchTitle] fired; response notes multiple versions/adaptations (1984/2021/2024).
results.reply:
"Dune" (1984), directed by David Lynch, is a sci-fi adventure film based on Frank Herbert's novel.
